TECHNIC-ARTICULATED COASTER-TRACK RAIL — the main coaster spine built from 13L Technic-beams cross-tied with 1×2 brick sleepers, slope-brick cars riding pin-jointed bogies through a banking heel-over turn, the whole engineering grammar readable tableside.

ROTATING FERRIS-WHEEL HUB — a Ferris wheel centred on a 12T Technic-axle hub with 11L beam-spokes radiating to an outer 16×16 ring, free-swinging gondola-cabins on clip-pivots hanging plumb, the classic working-wheel silhouette dominating the skyline.

GBC-STYLE CAROUSEL DRIVE-TRAIN — a carousel platform riding a visible worm-gear + 40T crown-gear train with a looped drive-belt suggesting Power-Functions motion, horse-mounts on cam-driven 3L bar-poles that bob as the deck turns, a kinetic AFOL centrepiece.

TRANS-ELEMENT NEON ENTRY ARCH — the ride-entry arch outlined in trans-red + trans-yellow 4L bar-elements slotted into 1×1 clip-bricks, with 1×1 trans-orange round-plates dotting every cornice like buzzing bulbs, a brick-built carnival blaze.

SNOT COASTER VERTICAL LOOP — a full 360° coaster loop built with 1×2 SNOT bracket-plates rotating the Technic-beam track rail through the vertical, a slope-brick car frozen at the apex, the physics-defying geometry the room stops to photograph.

CREATOR-EXPERT CANOPY FILIGREE — a carousel canopy built with overlapping 2×2 curved-slope bricks in cream + gold, lattice-work 1×4 bar-grille elements, pearl-gold printed-tile rosette medallions, and 1×1 cone finials, every edge speaking vintage-fairground opulence.

MICRO-CROWD MINIFIG MASSING — the park concourse packed with forty-plus standard minifigs in mismatched torsos and hat-pieces queuing, eating, pointing, the sheer density of colour and pose giving the whole layout a breathing, populated-park scale.

TRANS-BLUE FLUME WATER-CHANNEL — the flume ride channelled in overlapping trans-blue + trans-light-blue 2×8 plates banked on angled bracket-plates, white 1×1 round-plates clustered at the drop-base as foam-splash, a layered-trans splashdown pool alive with refracted light.

PRINTED-TILE RIDE-MARQUEE BOARD — the roller-coaster name-board assembled from period-font printed 2×2 tiles on a 45° slope-brick frame flanked by 1×1 round-plate bulb-string borders, every glyph crisp, the finishing-touch signage that conventions bend close to read.

MODULAR FAIRGROUND BASE-GRID — the park footprint laid on interlocking 32×32 baseplates with brick-built cobble-path lanes in tan + dark-tan, stall-modules and planter-builds slotting onto shared stud-rows, a fully expandable AFOL modular-fairground system.

DROP-TOWER TECHNIC GUIDE-RAIL — a drop-tower column built from stacked 2×2 round-bricks with a 9L Technic-beam guide-rail on each face, the seat-carriage riding Technic-pin followers, a taut 3L bar-element implying the lift-cable, the plunge geometry unmistakable.

TRANS-ELEMENT NIGHT-SHOW LIGHT-BANK — a ride-facade dressed in a grid of mixed trans-green + trans-purple + trans-orange 1×1 round-plates and 2L bar-elements in alternating rows, the programmed-looking colour-matrix suggesting a synchronised light-show frozen mid-sequence.

SNOT COASTER HELIX CURVE — a rising helix section built with successive SNOT bracket-plates rotating the Technic-beam spine 15° per module, slope-brick cars leaning into the bank, the ascending spiral reading as true three-dimensional track-geometry in brick.

WORM-GEAR FERRIS-WHEEL DRIVE — the Ferris wheel's axle driven by a visible 20T worm-gear meshing a 40T Technic-gear under the boarding platform, a drive-belt linking to a Power-Functions-implied motor housing, the whole drivetrain an open-engineering centrepiece.

CHASE-LIGHT BULB-STRING CANOPY — the carousel roof-ring edged with a continuous strand of alternating trans-yellow + trans-red 1×1 round-plates clipped to 1×1 plate-with-bar brackets, the looping chase-light string giving every night-mode photograph its fairground soul.

LATTICE ROLLER-COASTER SUPPORT TRESTLE — the coaster lift-hill trestle built from 1×2 Technic-beam cross-bracing in an X-lattice pattern, dark-red 1×1 round-bricks as rivet-nodes at every joint, the open steelwork silhouette towering over the surrounding stalls.

CLIP-PIVOT GONDOLA SUSPENSION — Ferris-wheel gondola-cabins each built on a 1×2 clip-hinge plate pivoting on a bar-element spoke-end, the cabins free to swing level under gravity, trans-clear 1×2 window-plates glazing each cab, a working-physics gondola build.

ORNATE TICKET-BOOTH FACADE — a carnival ticket-booth fronted with 1×2 printed-tile cash-counter panels, scalloped 2×2 curved-slope cornice bricks in bright-red, pearl-gold 1×1 tile price-boards, and a trans-yellow 1×2 window-brick cashier-window, the period detail immaculate.

TRANS-CLEAR COASTER-RAIL HIGHLIGHT — the coaster's outer safety-rail built from 4L trans-clear bar-elements clipped along the Technic-beam spine, light catching the rod in every photograph, the translucency making the engineering read as both structural and luminous.

CAM-DRIVEN HORSE UP-DOWN POLE — each carousel horse-mount riding a 2L Technic-axle through an offset 2×2 round-plate cam so the figure bobs one stud vertically per rotation, the mechanism exposed under the deck as an intentional kinetic-engineering display.

STALL-MODULE INTERLOCKING SYSTEM — individual fairground stalls built on 16×16 plate sub-bases with headlocking anti-stud rails on two edges, dropping onto path-baseplate stud-rows so the whole fairground reconfigures between display days, a clean AFOL modular-build grammar.

SCALLOPED COASTER-STATION CANOPY — the boarding-station roof built in overlapping 2×4 curved-slope bricks in alternating coral + cream rows, 1×1 cone finial peaks at each gable, gold 1×2 printed-tile border-strips, the Creator-Expert station facade earning every convention ribbon.

TRANS-BLUE FOUNTAIN BASIN — the park's central fountain built as a 32-stud circular well of layered trans-blue 2×2 round-plates rising to a 1×1 trans-clear round-plate jet, white 1×1 round-plates as water-droplet scatter, the still-water illusion surprisingly convincing.

DRIVE-BELT EXPOSED MECHANISM FEATURE — the ride machinery housing left deliberately open-sided with a looped rubber drive-belt running between a 16T Technic-gear and an 8T pinion, grey Technic-beam framing the housing, the working-guts visibility the signature AFOL motion-build move.

PRINTED-TILE HEIGHT-CHART QUEUE-POST — the ride-queue entrance finished with a 1×6 tile height-chart printed-tile stack on a 2×2 round-brick post, a minifig standing beside it for scale, a 1×2 printed rule-tile at eye-level, the storytelling micro-detail that judges always notice.
